messages:
Maya (Eng): Hey team - quick logistics q. Starting 2026-06-01 I'm going to be splitting my time between SF (home) and Reno (partner's place) on a 3-month trial: Mon-Wed in SF, Thu-Fri in Reno. Two asks: 1) How does WFH stipend work for a split-week? 2) Any payroll/state withholding changes? Also can Facilities coordinate sending a second monitor to Reno so I don't lug stuff back and forth?
Jordan (People Ops): Thanks Maya. Short answers: 1) We prorate WFH stipend by days at primary declared homebase vs temporary addresses. For a split-week pilot we'll pro-rate based on the days you spend in each location in the month. 2) Payroll: since Reno is NV and SF is CA, state withholding rules depend on days spent. CA has "convenience of employer" rules for some, but for split-week domestic short-term we typically adjust withholding if someone spends >30 consecutive days in another state or if they change their declared homebase.
Maya (Eng): Got it. So because it's alternating weekly it's not >30 straight days anywhere, right?
Ravi (Payroll): Correct on consecutive days. Alternating weeks should not trigger automatic state withholding change for CA vs NV as long as your declared homebase remains CA. That said, NV has no state income tax; we do need to record your temporary address for payroll reporting. If the pattern becomes permanent or you update homebase we will need a new W-4-like state form.
Saanvi (Benefits): On benefits: your health plan continues based on your homebase enrollment (SF/CA). For provider access in Reno, check telehealth and out-of-network coverage—some plans have limited in-person coverage out of state. If you expect to see providers in Reno regularly, ping me and we'll check network.
Maya (Eng): Thanks. About shipping monitor: can Facilities send a monitor to Reno and leave it there for the 3 months? Or do we need to process equipment check-out/in each week?
Leo (Facilities): We can ship a second monitor for temporary use. We treat it as a temporary assignment; please select "temporary equipment" in the relocate/asset form so it's tagged. We'll arrange delivery and pickup if you decide to return it after the pilot. No photos needed, recipient signature required.
Maya (Eng): Sweet. Any impact on commuter benefits or office perk eligibility since I'm in SF part of week?
Jordan (People Ops): Commuter pre-tax benefits are tied to commute into SF office; if you commute into SF office days, you remain eligible. Please record office in/out days on the schedule tool so facilities and payroll can validate.
Ravi (Payroll): One admin note: if you ever cross 30 consecutive days in NV, payroll will auto-generate a state withholding adjustment. Also if you start claiming Reno as your tax home we'll need updated tax forms.
Maya (Eng): Understood. Also curious if split-week affects WFH stipend caps or equipment reimbursement policy?
Jordan (People Ops): WFH stipend caps still apply monthly. For split-week we calculate stipend = (homebase days * full-homebase-rate + other days * other-location-rate) / days-in-month. Equipment reimbursements are per-employee per-year; temporary equipment requests follow Facilities approval, not the stipend budget.
Maya (Eng): Cool. One last: happy path if pilot goes permanent and I move my homebase to Reno?
Jordan (People Ops): If permanent, submit homebase-change form, we'll update payroll withholding, benefits residency rules, and equipment shipping/returns. Legal may need to review for nexus if multiple employees start moving to NV, but individual moves are normal.
legal-bot: Automated note: company-level nexus thresholds vary by state and activity. People Ops will notify Legal for any sustained cluster of homebase changes or new office setup.
Maya (Eng): Perfect, thanks for the clarity. I'll file the temporary-equipment and temporary-address forms and post my weekly office schedule.
Leo (Facilities): Got it - watch for a confirmation DM for delivery timing.
Saanvi (Benefits): Ping me after you submit forms if you want us to check provider directory for Reno zip.
Maya (Eng): Will do, thanks all! :wave:
